newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary electricity distributors offered 18.3pct hike - EDF.
newsitem.headline: Hungary electricity distributors offered 18.3pct hike - EDF.

text.p: Hungary's regional electricity distributing companies, in which Western utilities hold large stakes, have been told the government plans to allow them to raise the price they sell on their power by 18.3 percent from January 1.

"The forecast figure of 18.3 percent came from the Hungarian Energy Office and MVM (the Hungarian electricity company)," Electricite de France (EDF) representative in Hungary Pierre Abou told Reuters.
EDF has just under 50 percent stakes in two regional electricity distribution companies in Hungary.

The government announced two weeks ago retail hikes of 24.9 percent for electricity and 18.8 percent for gas but did not define the margins which would be granted to energy producers and distributors, in which Western utilities invested over $2 billion last year.
The Hungarian Energy Office said the government would announce the margins for suppliers and distributors in mid-December. @
Companies such as EDF and German electricity group RWE , which bought into the gas distribution network, were promised an eight percent return on investment from January 1997.

Abou said that such a large difference between purchasing prices and retail prices would generate no more than a four-per-cent profit margin for 1997 for the two companies, DEMASZ and EDASZ, in which EDF has stakes of just over 47 percent. @

"Definitely these conditions for purchasing and selling are unacceptable to us," he said. "This increase is equivalent to much below eight percent, maybe less than four with considerable contraint on operating conditions."
Abou said he hoped that further negotiation with the government would persuade them to set a higher margin when finally fixing the tariffs.
